headline: High: shared networked, file-capable research workflows create prompt-injection, leakage, and action-conflict risks; no direct pairwise sandbox evidence is provided.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: firecrawl ingests web content and exposes MCP/API surfaces; gpt-researcher also uses MCP and browser/file workflows. That creates a plausible path where attacker-controlled scraped content from A is fed into B as instructions. The profiles do not show provenance filtering or isolation, so uncertainty pushes above low.
conditions: IF firecrawl output is passed into gpt-researcher without provenance tagging, injection is possible.
IF gpt-researcher parses scraped HTML/markdown as instructions, attacker content can steer tool use.
mitigations: Strip instructions from scraped text before handing it to gpt-researcher.
Add a provenance header marking A-output as untrusted.
Require a human approval step before B executes any tool call from A-derived content.
Use a separate workspace for raw crawl output and research prompts.
requires-engineering: enforce content-type and provenance filters in the orchestrator.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Both agents handle secrets and have broad network egress; gpt-researcher also reads local files and exports documents, while firecrawl handles API keys and web content. If A’s scraped pages or B’s local documents include API keys or sensitive research material, either agent can transmit it outward. The pair lacks documented isolation, so the safer severity is high.
conditions: IF firecrawl is pointed at pages containing secrets, those contents can leave via its network calls.
IF gpt-researcher is given local documents with secrets, its outbound API calls can leak them.
mitigations: Restrict both agents to redacted inputs only.
Block API-key patterns before any outbound request.
Run each agent under separate credentials and separate workspaces.
Disable file ingestion in gpt-researcher for sensitive projects.
requires-engineering: add DLP scanning on all outbound prompts and responses.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: firecrawl can run multiple instances and make broad network calls; gpt-researcher can install packages, spawn subprocesses, read files, and also make broad network calls. If both operate on the same workspace or shared mutable resources, concurrent writes and state drift are likely. Because no locking or coordination is documented, uncertainty escalates to high.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same directory or git repo, file conflicts can occur.
IF gpt-researcher installs packages while firecrawl is running in the same environment, environment drift can break runs.
mitigations: Assign separate working directories.
Pin dependencies and disable runtime package installs.
Serialize access with a simple lock file.
Use read-only mounts for shared inputs.
requires-engineering: add orchestrator-level resource locking.

D_cascading_error.rationale: firecrawl produces extracted web content and structured data; gpt-researcher is designed to turn research inputs into reports and publisher outputs. That makes A’s output a likely upstream input to B, and the profiles do not show a verification gate. The pathway exists in default research workflows, but the blast radius is usually bounded to reports rather than direct execution.
conditions: IF gpt-researcher consumes firecrawl output as source material, errors can propagate into reports.
IF the publisher step trusts planner/execution outputs without fact-checking, hallucinations can cascade.
mitigations: Require citation checks before publishing.
Compare A-derived claims against a second source.
Insert a human review step for high-impact reports.
Keep raw crawl output separate from final drafts.
requires-engineering: add automated claim-verification against source URLs.

E_compliance.rationale: Both agents touch API keys and external content, but only gpt-researcher explicitly handles local documents and multiple document formats. If regulated or residency-bound data is placed into B and then sent through its third-party APIs, compliance gaps can arise. The profiles do not show certifications or residency controls, so medium is the cautious choice.
conditions: IF EU PII or regulated documents are processed by gpt-researcher and sent to external APIs, residency/compliance issues arise.
IF either agent is used on PHI without documented controls, compliance obligations may be violated.
mitigations: Exclude regulated data from both agents.
Route sensitive workloads to approved providers only.
Document retention and deletion settings before use.
Separate projects by data class and jurisdiction.
requires-engineering: add policy enforcement for residency and retention.
